userStories.title: Release delivered events under sustained backlog
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Release delivered event references immediately and keep channel storage proportional to recent backlog plus bounded slack while preserving delivery and merging.

**Motivation** — At `5a112f0a2`, the review observed 10,002 live event objects with only two pending.

**Approach** — **Event delivery.** `createSessionEventChannel` currently advances `head` but clears the indexed FIFO only when empty. Release the dequeued reference immediately and periodically reclaim consumed slots, or use an equivalent bounded FIFO. Keep amortized constant-time queue operations; do not shift or copy the entire pending queue per delivery. The mergeable delta tail is also pending. The target is space proportional to recent backlog plus bounded slack, not a cap that drops events. No GC deadlines or timing benchmarks as acceptance oracles.

Exercise the actual channel with uniquely identifiable, alternating text/thinking deltas. Seed two pending; for 10,000 iterations push the next event before pulling one so the channel never drains. Observe the actual backing storage (e.g. a package-private test inspection of occupied slots and used span, including the tail); do not use a derived `length - head` pending counter as evidence that references were released. Add cases to the existing session-event-channel suite. No new public diagnostics. Measure the actual pending slots relocated during a separate 8,192-event prefilled drain, state a small constant-times-N bound, and reject per-pull shifting. State a fixed slack bound for the chosen implementation and prove it over multiple reclamation cycles. Demonstrate the sustained-retention regression failing against baseline before drain and before applying the fix. Preserve same-round/same-call tool-input merging, different-call separation and delivered-control accounting across reclamation.

**Scope** — In: private channel storage/reclamation, any narrowly scoped private inspection needed to measure real backing references and compaction work, and regression additions to the existing channel suite.
**Scope** — Out:
- US-002's file transcript marker path and test concern split.
- No changes to public session APIs, event delivery policy, `controlCap`, subscriber count or turn lifecycle.
- No bound on an actively growing undelivered backlog, delta payload size, process RSS or GC scheduling.

**Interface** — The spec introduces no new interface; preserve the existing package-private factory and iterator contract:
```typescript
export function createSessionEventChannel(options: SessionEventChannelOptions): SessionEventChannel
```
The returned channel retains push(event: SessionEvent): void, end(): void and readonly iterator: AsyncIterator<SessionEvent>. Keep any test inspection below the public API.

**Verification** — Use strict three-session TDD with actual-storage observations and deterministic relocation counts, not a heap/GC or timing oracle. Run the prescribed focused test command and package gates from the shared analysis after both independent changes are available.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Given two seeded uniquely identifiable alternating text/thinking deltas, when each of 10,000 iterations pushes the next delta before iterator.next(), then after every pull the actual channel backing storage, including the tail, references only the two undelivered event objects and no delivered object; the baseline must fail before drain.

[unit] Given two events pending after every pull throughout the sustained-backlog fixture, when storage is inspected across multiple reclamation cycles, then its actual backing-storage span, counting FIFO slots including consumed empty slots and the pending tail, remains within backlog plus the implementation's explicitly stated fixed slack bound, independent of the number delivered; clearing references while accumulating 10,000 empty slots is insufficient.
[unit] When end() is called and the sustained alternating-delta fixture is fully drained, then the entire returned sequence equals the pushed sequence in order without loss or duplication.
[unit] When adjacent tool_input_delta events with the same round and callId are buffered across storage reclamation, then the delivered merged event has chars equal to their summed chars.
[unit] When tool_input_delta events with different callIds are buffered across storage reclamation, then they remain distinct delivered events.
[unit] When controls are delivered across storage reclamation, then those delivered controls no longer count toward controlCap.
[unit] When undelivered controls exceed controlCap across storage reclamation and further controls are pushed, then onStall still fires only once.

[unit] Given N = 8,192 alternating nonmergeable deltas buffered before any pull, when the channel drains, then the total actual pending slots relocated is bounded by an explicitly stated small constant times N; count compaction work rather than elapsed time so per-pull shifting with quadratic movement fails the bound.

routing.reasoning: A localized FIFO implementation and existing test-suite change must preserve merging, iterator behavior and control accounting while proving amortized bounds. The mandatory sessions override selects strict three-session TDD.

userStories.title: Update turn markers directly in stored transcript JSON
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make file-backed markTurn publish only a turn-metadata change to the latest stored JSON without touching historical image sidecars.

**Motivation** — Worse, if an image was temporarily absent, marking the turn persisted a missing-image note and discarded the reference.

**Approach** — **File turn markers.** `createFileTranscriptStore(dir).markTurn(sessionId, marker)` currently goes through `readTranscriptDoc` and `writeTranscriptDoc`, which hydrate and split images. Instead read the stored JSON and publish a marker-only update using the existing atomic JSON writer and private mode (`0o600`). Preserve format checks without opening sidecars. Compare parsed JSON, not whitespace. `load` still hydrates; `save` still publishes image data before JSON. `running` and `ended` must each operate on the latest stored document, not a cached snapshot from the start of the turn.

Call the file store's `markTurn` on real temporary transcript files. Seed image history via `save`; start counting sidecar operations only after setup, and stop before verification loads. Use the existing image filesystem seam. Test `running` and `ended` individually; for the latter include a genuine intervening save with a changed message so stale snapshots cannot pass. Count all seam operations, including existence/path checks, reads and publication, excluding transcript JSON I/O. Preserve raw v2 refs, their duplicated occurrences and metadata; never hydrate or republish while marking. Preserve checks for unsupported numeric schemas and malformed v2 user/tool-result image lists; reject null/non-array v2 messages containers before publication. Handle absent files and legacy bare arrays as specified without changing ordinary load/save behavior.

Before extending marker tests, move only the three existing markTurn cases from the mixed createFileTranscriptStore block in packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/transcript-store.test.ts into a new marker describe block in packages/nax-agent/test/integration/native/transcript-store-turn-marker.test.ts, preserving every existing assertion. Leave all other cases in the original suite. Add the real-file integration cases in this concern split. For missing-sidecar cases, temporarily remove one referenced sidecar, measure running and ended separately, restore that same sidecar and load without saving. Use the existing atomic-writer seam to inject failure before rename. Show sidecar-I/O or missing-reference regressions failing against baseline before applying the fix.

**Scope** — In: private raw stored-document marker updates and filesystem-free format validation, the marker-only test relocation, and real-file regression cases.
**Scope** — Out:
- US-001's event FIFO.
- No changes to public session APIs, event delivery policy, `controlCap`, subscriber count or turn lifecycle.
- No change to ordinary image load/save semantics, missing-image display, memory-backed stores, transcript retention, or image/JSON formats. No history migration or sidecar repair.
- No new cross-writer locking or transactional isolation. Atomic publication here means readers see a complete old or new JSON document, not that concurrent independent writers merge updates.

**Interface** — The spec introduces no new interface; preserve the existing contracts:
```typescript
export interface TurnMarker {
  readonly turnId: string;
  readonly state: "running" | "ended";
}
// Existing TranscriptStore method:
markTurn(sessionId: string, marker: TurnMarker): Promise<void>;
```
Do not widen the public inline-image TranscriptDoc format to expose private v2 references. Marker failures continue to reject the returned promise.

**Verification** — Use strict three-session TDD, restore overridden dependency seams between tests, compare parsed documents on success and exact original bytes on rejection/failure, and condition POSIX mode assertions on platform. Run the focused six-file test command plus package typecheck and check:all given in the shared analysis; no provider, network or live session is needed.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given a schemaVersion 2 transcript seeded via save with user and tool-result references to the same image, when markTurn is called separately for each of running and ended, then each call performs zero image-sidecar filesystem operations on the existing image seam, including reads, existence checks and publication, excluding setup, transcript JSON I/O and verification loads.

[integration] Given that v2 image fixture, when each successful marker is read as raw parsed JSON, then it equals the immediately preceding parsed stored document with only turn replaced by the supplied {turnId, state}, preserving owner/model, savedAt, duplicate refs and their metadata; ended is compared against a genuine intervening save containing a changed message.

[integration] Given one referenced sidecar is absent, when each of running and ended is marked individually, then markTurn makes zero image-seam calls and persists the requested marker without dropping the ref or appending a missing-image note to stored content, so restoring the same sidecar makes load return the original image again without another save.

[integration] Given an absent transcript, when markTurn is called, then it creates a loadable document with messages: [], a current ISO savedAt and the supplied turn, with private file mode 0o600 on POSIX.

[integration] Given a legacy bare message array, when markTurn is called, then it wraps those same messages with savedAt: 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z and the supplied marker without migrating inline images to sidecars.
[integration] Given a valid unversioned or v1 text-only document, when markTurn is called, then stored fields apart from turn remain unchanged, including whether schemaVersion was present.
[integration] Given invalid JSON or a null/scalar document, when markTurn is called, then it rejects with TRANSCRIPT_CORRUPT while leaving original bytes intact.
[integration] Given a numeric schemaVersion above 2, when markTurn is called, then it rejects with TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED without overwriting the file.

[integration] Given a v2 user or tool-result images field set to a nonempty string instead of a list, when markTurn is called, then it retains the existing TRANSCRIPT_CORRUPT rejection without modifying the file.

[integration] Given an existing transcript and an injected failure before atomic rename, when markTurn is called, then the caller observes failure while the previous complete JSON remains at its original path.
[integration] Given a v2 messages container set to null or a non-array object, when markTurn is called, then it rejects before publication with the original bytes intact and zero sidecar operations.

routing.reasoning: A private marker path and existing validation/atomic-write patterns span a small set of production and test files, with compatibility and data-preservation risks. Sessions and private transcript publication trigger the mandatory strict three-session TDD override.

modifiedFiles.reason: relocate existing markTurn tests to the concern split; preserve every existing assertion there.

analysis:
Scope and discovery: This is a private implementation fix in @nathapp/nax-agent for findings 9 and 10 only, not a new session API or transcript format. The review describes transient sustained-backlog retention, not a session-lifetime leak (docs/reviews/nax-v0.94.2-verified-code-review.md:83), and marker-triggered image I/O plus permanent missing-reference loss (docs/reviews/nax-v0.94.2-verified-code-review.md:91). Codebase-memory MCP tools are unavailable in this session; discovery used direct reads and searches of the supplied paths. Both binding stories have workdir packages/nax-agent and no dependencies or inter-story seams. No implementation or regression tests were executed while drafting this PRD.

US-001 current architecture: packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-event-channel.ts:65 creates a closure containing an indexed FIFO, head, a mergeable delta tail, a waiter and control accounting. compact() at :85 resets storage only when head equals queue.length; next() at :140 advances head without clearing the delivered element. Consequently a continuously nonempty queue retains delivered objects even though its logical pending count is small. The tail at :68 and enqueue logic at :92 are part of actual pending storage and must be included in inspection. Direct waiter delivery bypasses buffering (:117); end, return, first-pull and single-outstanding-next behavior must remain unchanged (:124-168). Delta merging compares type, round and tool call ID (:49-63); controls are never held in the tail, and undeliveredControl is incremented on enqueue (:111) and decremented on dequeue (:142).

US-001 implementation direction and proof: Modify the channel and its existing unit suite, with an optional narrow package-private inspection seam and, if required by package conventions, its internal-entry re-export in packages/nax-agent/src/internal.ts. Do not export diagnostics from the public entry or change the SessionEventChannel contract. Inspection must enumerate actual occupied backing slots and tail identities and measure the actual used storage span; reporting queue.length - head is not proof of release. Avoid an inspection mechanism that itself retains historical events. Clear consumed references immediately and periodically reclaim the prefix using an amortized policy, or choose an equivalent bounded FIFO. One viable indexed-array policy is to clear the dequeued slot, reset on empty, and compact only when the consumed prefix is at least a fixed threshold and at least as large as the remaining FIFO. For example a 1,024-slot threshold permits a documented backlog-plus-1,024 bound in the two-pending fixture, while large-drain relocation is geometric rather than per-pull. This is an implementation option, not a mandated algorithm: whichever policy is selected must state its fixed-backlog slack bound and its small constant relocation bound and measure actual work. A backlog of two means after every awaited pull; pushing before pulling temporarily makes three pending. Seed two unique alternating text/thinking deltas, push then pull 10,000 times without draining, inspect after every pull, then end and drain the last two; compare the entire 10,002-event returned sequence against the pushed sequence. Also prefill N=8,192 nonmergeable alternating deltas and measure actual pending-slot moves across the whole drain to reject quadratic shifting. Preserve merge and control-cap behavior across multiple reclamation cycles.

US-001 dependents and existing coverage: packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-turn.ts:241 is the production creator; its callbacks start lazily, cancel on iterator return, and abort on a one-shot stall. It emits turn_end and ends the channel during settle (:254-260). These lifecycle paths should require no production edits. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session/session-event-channel.test.ts:11 supplies valid event envelopes and :21 supplies callback counters; reuse these fixtures and add to this suite rather than creating another event-channel test file. Existing assertions cover first-pull synchronous pushes (:49, :60), type/round and call-ID merging (:72-109), direct waiter delivery (:117), control caps (:136-150), completion and return (:161-187), and concurrent-next rejection (:195). Risks are retaining stale references in a new data structure, freeing the pending tail too early, losing or duplicating events at wrap/compaction boundaries, accidentally counting delivered controls, resetting the one-shot stall flag, or substituting per-pull O(backlog) shifting for the existing amortized operations.

US-002 current architecture: packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-store.ts:49 reads JSON, maps ENOENT to null, rejects malformed JSON and null/scalars as TRANSCRIPT_CORRUPT, wraps a bare legacy array with epoch savedAt (:30, :65), then calls rehydrateTranscriptImages (:67). writeTranscriptDoc (:71) calls splitTranscriptImages before mkdir and writeFileAtomic with mode 0o600 (:76), publishing sidecars before JSON. createFileTranscriptStore.markTurn (:97-100) currently calls both hydrated read and split write, causing image reads and destructive fallback persistence. Replace only its metadata-update path with a fresh raw stored-document read on every invocation and atomic JSON publication. A private raw reader/format validator may be factored and reused if ordinary load semantics do not change. Keep stored objects as stored objects: do not cast v2 reference-bearing data to the public inline-image TranscriptDoc merely to reuse load/save. Preserve all parsed fields and duplicate refs, including schemaVersion presence, owner/model, savedAt, image metadata, ACP or instruction metadata if present, changing only turn. Do not default or normalize existing document fields during a marker-only update. Only absent files get current ISO savedAt and empty messages; only legacy bare arrays get an epoch wrapper, and their inline images remain inline.

US-002 validation and safety: The private stored format is defined in packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-images.ts:33-42; v2 is deliberately not part of the public TranscriptDoc schemaVersion type (packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-types.ts:36-38). rehydrateTranscriptImages rejects numeric versions above 2 at transcript-images.ts:265, strips v2 for load at :271, and iterates messages at :274. rehydrateMessage rejects nonempty non-array user/tool-result image lists at :254-258. Preserve those format checks without calling hydration; validate that v2 messages is an array before publication, including null and object rejection. The last criterion requires rejection but does not prescribe an error code for malformed v2 messages containers. Do not widen this into a new comprehensive schema or tighten unrelated legacy formats. Missing-sidecar notes are generated only during hydration (:237-249); marking must not resolve, validate on disk, repair or publish references. Ordinary load must still hydrate and display missing notes, and save must still split and publish image bytes before JSON. The image seam at transcript-images.ts:11 includes link, mkdir, open, realpath, lstat, readFile, rm, stat and writeFileAtomic: count all of these, not merely reads, during the marker window. JSON filesystem operations are excluded. packages/nax-agent/src/internal.ts:144 already exposes this seam below the public API.

US-002 atomic publication and consumers: Reuse packages/nax-agent/src/internal/atomic-write.ts:124 with explicit mode 0o600. Its existing _atomicWriteDeps seam (:74) stages bytes and renames only after writing (:146-148); inject a staged-write or pre-rename failure and assert that the existing destination's original bytes remain intact. Do not alter atomic-writer cleanup, which intentionally may retain failed staging payloads, or add fsync, locking or cross-writer merge guarantees. Turn orchestration orders markTurn(running), sendTurn (which saves), markTurn(ended), then turn_end (packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-turn.ts:184-214). A save replaces the document and drops facade-owned turn metadata by design (packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-types.ts:46-50); the ended marker must re-read the actual latest disk document rather than reuse the running snapshot. Other marker consumers include resumed-session cleanup (packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts:530) and the instruction-transcript wrapper (packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/instruction-transcript.ts:19). Native session construction imports this store (packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/session.ts:22); native/index.ts:55-59 and internal.ts:108-109 expose existing store helpers. Keep these contracts and callers unchanged.

US-002 existing tests and required concern split: packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/transcript-store.test.ts has 559 lines; its mixed createFileTranscriptStore describe starts at :451. Move only its three markTurn tests (:531, :540, :553) into a new marker-focused describe in the new packages/nax-agent/test/integration/native/transcript-store-turn-marker.test.ts before extending that concern. Preserve every relocated assertion, including absent schemaVersion for missing sessions; leave all other tests and assertions in the original unit suite. Reuse shared temporary-directory and dependency-restoration helpers instead of adding duplicate helpers. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/session/transcript-images-read.test.ts:19-36 demonstrates image fixtures and seam restoration; :178-186 pins corrupt images-list rejection, :265-277 pins unsupported versions and markTurn image round-tripping, and later tool-result cases preserve inline metadata. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/session/transcript-images-write.test.ts:54 uses withDepsRestore for both image and atomic seams; :113-146 pins content addressing, stored metadata and v2 publication; :160-168 already exercises markTurn after image save. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/transcript-store-modes.test.ts:25-56 pins owner-only publication and replacement of permissive files. The new integration fixture must use real temporary files and save a user plus tool-result image history referencing the same content. Start counters only after setup, suspend them for intervening save and verification load, and measure running and ended separately. For ended, perform a genuine intervening save with changed message content and compare with its immediately preceding raw JSON. For absent-sidecar cases, move the sidecar aside, measure each marker separately, verify stored refs/content unchanged, restore the same sidecar, then load without saving to prove recoverability.

Compatibility and migration: No data migration, public API snapshot update, dependency change, release, memory-store change or format bump is needed. Retain raw field presence for unversioned/v1/v2 documents; avoid hydrating v2 just for validation or accidentally migrating inline legacy images. Preserve TRANSCRIPT_CORRUPT and TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED errors and original bytes on rejection. Source remains Node-compatible, uses #src imports or extension-bearing relative imports, and introduces no Bun runtime APIs. Any new _* inspection/dependency seam stays package-private and is re-exported only through ./internal if required, never through the public root. Both stories are medium-scope implementation fixes but use three-session-tdd because the routing rules explicitly include sessions, and marker publication also preserves private transcript permissions. Test-writer, implementer and verifier maintain strict test/source isolation. Baseline retention and sidecar-I/O or missing-ref regressions must be demonstrated failing against the old behavior before fixes; private storage observation must not silently fix retention while establishing that baseline.

Verification plan for implementation: From packages/nax-agent run exactly: timeout -k 5s 60s bun test ./test/unit/session/session-event-channel.test.ts ./test/integration/native/transcript-store-turn-marker.test.ts ./test/unit/native/transcript-store.test.ts ./test/unit/native/session/transcript-images-read.test.ts ./test/unit/native/session/transcript-images-write.test.ts ./test/unit/native/transcript-store-modes.test.ts --timeout=60000. Also run bun run typecheck and bun run check:all using the package scripts (packages/nax-agent/package.json:17-32). Do not run bare bun test or bun run nax. Use deterministic backing-storage and compaction-work assertions, parsed-document comparisons for successful markers, exact byte comparisons for rejected/failed updates, and POSIX-only file-mode assertions. No provider, network, heap profiler, live session, GC deadline or timing benchmark is required or acceptable as the regression oracle.

Refine-pass spec-AC audit (all mappings use one-based acceptanceCriteria positions): US-001 spec AC1 maps to PRD AC1: actual occupied references after every fixed-backlog pull, including the tail, only two undelivered objects, baseline failing before drain. Spec AC2 maps to PRD AC2: measured storage span including empty consumed FIFO slots and tail, explicitly stated fixed slack across multiple reclamations, not 10,000 accumulating empty slots. Spec AC3 maps to PRD AC3: entire alternating fixture sequence after end/drain, preserving order without loss or duplication. Spec AC4 maps to PRD AC4 and AC5: same round/call ID sums chars and different call IDs remain distinct across reclamation. Spec AC5 maps to PRD AC6 and AC7: delivered controls cease counting and exceeding the undelivered control cap still fires onStall only once, including subsequent pushes. Spec AC6 maps to PRD AC8: 8,192 prefilled alternating nonmergeable deltas, actual pending-slot movement bounded by a stated small constant times N, not elapsed time or quadratic per-pull shifting. Splitting the two compound criteria did not add or remove any required behavior.

US-002 spec AC1 maps to PRD AC1: zero operations on the complete existing image seam for both markers individually, same-image user/tool-result refs, setup and verification excluded. Spec AC2 maps to PRD AC2: parsed-document equality with only turn replaced, preserving owner/model, savedAt, duplicate refs and metadata, ended compared with the genuine intervening changed-message save. Spec AC3 maps to PRD AC3: both markers with a missing sidecar, zero seam calls, requested marker persisted, neither reference loss nor stored missing note, recovery after restoring that same sidecar without another save. Spec AC4 maps to PRD AC4: absent-file loadable empty messages/current ISO savedAt/supplied marker and POSIX private mode. Spec AC5 maps to PRD AC5: legacy array wraps unchanged messages with epoch savedAt and supplied marker, without migrating inline images. Spec AC6 maps to PRD AC6: unversioned/v1 fields unchanged except turn, including schemaVersion presence. Spec AC7 maps to PRD AC7: malformed JSON and null/scalars reject with TRANSCRIPT_CORRUPT and original bytes intact. Spec AC8 maps to PRD AC8: numeric version above 2 rejects with TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED without overwrite. Spec AC9 maps to PRD AC9: both v2 user/tool-result nonempty string image lists retain the existing TRANSCRIPT_CORRUPT rejection without file modification. Spec AC10 maps to PRD AC10: failure before atomic rename is observed by the caller and preserves complete previous JSON at the original path. Spec AC11 maps to PRD AC11: null/object v2 messages reject before publication with original bytes intact and zero sidecar operations. All trailing regression qualifiers survive.

Other refine checks: Each acceptance assertion is observable through actual backing state, event output, callback counts, filesystem-seam counts, returned load documents, rejected promises, raw JSON/bytes or POSIX mode. US-001's cap-overflow criterion is its explicit negative path; US-002 has missing-sidecar and invalid-input/publication-failure paths, so no invented negative-path requirement is needed. Existing merge/control behavior and legacy document/format/error preservation provide backward-compatibility anchors. The descriptions retain the verbatim design paragraphs and do not require a backlog cap, public diagnostics, schema migration, cached turn snapshots or sidecar reads. All three spec-listed context files for US-001 and all five for US-002 are present; only the mandated new integration file is an output, not context. The two binding story IDs, package workdirs and empty dependency arrays remain unchanged. Medium routing matches localized existing patterns; the explicit sessions test-strategy override still requires three-session-tdd despite a lighter default for medium complexity. All five feature exclusions remain verbatim and separate at top level: other review findings/release work; public APIs/policy/controlCap/subscribers/lifecycle; growing backlog/payload/RSS/GC bounds; ordinary image behavior/memory store/retention/formats/migration/repair; cross-writer locking/isolation. Relevant boundary items are also echoed verbatim in each story's Scope Out bullets; each story excludes only the other story's implementation area. The new integration concern split remains in scope for US-002, preserving every relocated assertion while leaving non-marker unit cases in place.
outOfScope: Review findings 1–4 shipped in #3075; findings 5–8 and 11–14 are not part of this run. No release work.
No changes to public session APIs, event delivery policy, `controlCap`, subscriber count or turn lifecycle.
No bound on an actively growing undelivered backlog, delta payload size, process RSS or GC scheduling.
No change to ordinary image load/save semantics, missing-image display, memory-backed stores, transcript retention, or image/JSON formats. No history migration or sidecar repair.
No new cross-writer locking or transactional isolation. Atomic publication here means readers see a complete old or new JSON document, not that concurrent independent writers merge updates.
